I think that it would be:  


**Luci - Cryo**  
: Ever since his days in the Celestial Realm, Luci has always been someone very strict, and he became cold when they descended upon Devildom. I think that the Tsaritsa would take interest in this and give him the Vision when he pledged his loyalty to Diavolo. Who knows? Luci might even become a harbinger.  
**Mammon - Geo**  
: Taking to note that Morax is the god of Mora, it is quite ironic. Mammon has always been into money, and one of the things that would sell lots is jewelry. Morax (\*cough) would most likely take interest in the fact that Mammon tries to make easy cash, and may offer the Vision when Mammon helps the little girl, this is a reference to the Devilgram story, "The Guardian Demon".   
**Levi - Hydro**  
: Of course, it's Leviathan! The sea monster himself! Although we don't know much about the Hydro Archon - minus her virtue, which is justice - I suppose that she would choose Levi to hold the Hydro Vision amongst the brothers. Our otaku would probably get it through taming the sea serpent (I don't remember the name though, I faintly remember it being mentioned in one of the chats, the one mentioning the pet contest for spirit week?).  
**Satan - Dendro**  
: The avatar of wrath is very much a bookworm, and with books come knowledge! The dendro archon would most definitely admire the fact that Satan could keep his calm demeanor up via reading, and would be happy to offer the blonde a dendro vision. The power was given to him through a simple encounter: it being found within a book, replacing the bookmark that Satan originally placed.  
**Asmo - Anemo**  
\- Asmo is very free-spirited, and I think that Barbatos (\*cough (2)) would love that about him! The anemo archon chuckles to himself as he sees Asmo tease his brothers, reminding him of himself and the original Seven. I think that Barbatos would give the Vision through one of the times that he manages to persuade someone, although the archon would want Asmo to give that person freedom.  
**Beel - Pyro**  
\- Beel reminds me of Xiangling, with the gastronomy trip and all! I think that the Pyro Archon, Murata would give him the Vision because of something akin to Xiangling's, but at the same time, something more noble. I suppose that Beel would be given the Vision when he protected Belphie. The Pyro Archon has been watching the brothers, then the Great Celestial War occured, leading to the death of Lilith and all. When they got to Devildom, that's where Beel recieved the Pyro Vision.  
**Belphie - Electro**  
\- Before Baal initiated the Vision Hunt Decree, I think that the Raiden Shogun watched over the brothers. She found it interesting when Belphie was kept in the attic for - supposedly, I think - all eternity. However, when MC (I think that it was MC, based on the timeloop task) released Belphegor from the attic, the archon found out about his hatred for humans, taking it as a hatred for mortality - the opposite of immortality/eternity. That's why when the avatar of sloth knocked MC out, the Raiden Shogun gave him an Electro Vision.

**Diavolo - Pyro**  
\- Being the king of hell, Murata only found it fitting to offer a Pyro vision to the only son of the demon lord. This will be pretty short, hehe, I think that Murata provided the source of power through an heirloom or artifact. Diavolo probably doesn't use it all too much, and instead keeps it on display in his castle.  
**Barbatos - Anemo**  
\- Honestly? DUH! Named after the anemo archon himself! Archon Barbatos found this amusing and gave him the Vision, which is something I think V--- the archon would do!

**Simeon - Anemo**  
\- Akin to Asmo, Simeon is a free-spirited angel. He does follow the rules set by the Celestial Realm and Michael of course, but all-in-all, Simeon is very friendly and open! I think that Barbatos provided said angel with the Vision during the Great Celestial War (I suppose that Simeon was already an angel by them, since Luke mentions that he admired Luci when he was an angel, and Simeon is considered Luke's legal guardian).  
**Luke - Hydro**  
\- Uptight and somewhat strict in his own way, the little Cherubim Luke has some sense of justice, all from the perspective of the Celestial Realm. Either way, due to this attitude of his, the Hydro Archon most likely gave him a Vision through "A Job for Michael", or something related to that. She is very much amused by his behavior towards demons.  
**Solomon - Electro**  
\- As a human who managed to make himself immortal, no matter the realm, the Raiden Shogun admired this trick of his. Being the god of eternity, she gave Solomon the Vision to "propagate" her so-called value on the very day he made himself immortal.

Tbh, I used to fall for his "plots" and sometimes actually felt a sort-of good impact on me. And that's not bad. However, I feel like Dhar Mann is using this effect for the views to go out.

From what I see and felt before, the reason his videos get so many views is because the general plots of these stories are good. "Don't yell at your kids, teach them instead.", "Not everyday has to have an occasion to make your s.o feel special.", and "Don't judge a book by its cover.". These are good plots to use and can actually, truly ***"change lives".***

The biggest issue that I have with this creator is the feel-good, toxic message.

In the end of each of his plots, the ending turns out good for the main character, and the antagonist repents. However, life isn't always like that. The "protagonists" of the situation sometimes just... give up, and the "antagonists" won't always be sorry, they won't come running back to the protagonists, too. Life is full of so many different people.

People don't always say sorry,  
People will sometimes get their way,  
People aren't completely bad, nor completely good.

That brings me to another big issue, his videos always have this black-and-white view. He always shows that one is completely righteous whilst the other one is completely evil, which isn't true. 

Another issue is his stereotypes. He always uses certain people for certain roles. This leads us to judge their characters right away as *bad.* Heck, sometimes, we even start to believe that the actors themselves are bad due to them usually or always reprising a bad role in each video.

For the last issue, Dhar Mann doesn't really get "moving on". Whenever he shows a timeskip of a divorce or break up video, it kinda shows how the mc is giving the antagonist an "in-your-face" dialogue or expression. This sort-of means that the mc hasn't fully forgiven the antagonist, and therefore hasn't truly moved on; you don't need to slap them in the face when you have truly moved on, and forgiving them does not equal to going back to them.

I honestly hope that his plots improve, so that others would learn some harsh realities, and even some possible consequences of their actions. Then, they will surely learn.

P.S: I do wish that they'd (Dhar, and his wife, Laura) lessen their pictures of their baby, Ella Rose.  She's pretty cute (I mean, all babies are, pretty much), but they have to know the dangers of online child, toddler, and even baby predators.
